support_convention: full lattice points of the two Newton polygons

system_size.note: det J - x^2 has exactly as many monomials as det J, since (2,0) is in the support already

stage1_attainable_support.conclusion: (2,0) is attainable and its coefficient is exactly a1_0*b2_1, so det J = x^2 is NOT excluded by support.  EMPTY_BY_SUPPORT is ruled out.  Note that x | det J (min x-degree 1) while the y-only monomials (0,1),(0,2),... are NOT attainable: the naive 'det J is divisible by y' reading is wrong, because N(Q) has the vertex (2,1) and Q_y therefore carries the exponent (2,0).

stage2_lowest_x_degree_block.conclusion: The lowest-x-degree block is three equations in five unknowns. Its ideal is (a1_0 b1_1, a1_0 b1_2, a1_1 b1_2 - a1_2 b1_1), of dimension 3; adding a1_0 b2_1 = 1 keeps dimension 3. The block is satisfiable (e.g. b1_1 = b1_2 = 0, a1_1, a1_2 free, a1_0 b2_1 = 1), so it is not decisive.

rows.why: both edge forms are univariate in the same monomial (or one of them is a monomial), so the 2x2 Jacobian vanishes identically

rows.status: non-empty (not solved: 19 unknowns; reduced to the (F0) block in stage 5)

strict_chart.family: A = a*y^14*(y-r)^2, B = b*y^21*(y-r)^3 (all corner coefficients nonzero when a*b*r != 0)

rows.why: both edge forms are univariate in the same monomial (or one of them is a monomial), so the 2x2 Jacobian vanishes identically

stage3_weighted_valuations.conclusion: Every distinct edge weight gives a satisfiable (or vacuous) leading-form condition; none is empty.  No single-edge valuation yields a certificate of emptiness.

stage4_quasihomogeneous_reduction.identity: det J(P,Q) = u^2 * Jac_{z,u}(P,Q);  target x^2 = z^2 u^-4

five_equations.F2: -A' E - 2 C' D - 3 F' B + 2 A E' + C D' = 0
five_equations.F3: -C' E - 2 F' D + C E' + 2 A G' = 0

top_block.normalisation: A1(0) = 1 and B1(0) = 1 fix the scaling (A,B) -> (lam*A, B/lam) and the z^0 equation
top_block.degenerate_solution: A = z, B = z^2 (A1 = B1 = 1) satisfies (F0)
top_block.exact_family: A = lam*z, B = z^2/lam satisfies (F0) exactly for every lam != 0
top_block.solution_dimension_certificate: (F0) is invariant under (A,B) -> (lam*A, B/lam), and the explicit orbit A = lam*z, B = z^2/lam is a 1-parameter family of exact solutions, so the (F0) solution set has dimension >= 1.
top_block.strict_chart_edge_family: A = a*y^14*(y-r)^2, B = b*y^21*(y-r)^3 solves the (2,-1) leading form 8 A B' - 12 A' B = 0 exactly
top_block.status: non-empty as a system; the exact-degree (7,10) part is reduced to 6 equations in 7 unknowns and is NOT resolved

stage4_quasihomogeneous_reduction.conclusion: The system is exactly equivalent to (F0)-(F4); the top block (F0) reduces to 6 equations in 7 unknowns and admits the degenerate solution A = z, B = z^2.  No contradiction at this level.

stage5_x_adic_cascade.method: x-degree (== z-degree) ordered cascade.  Level 19 is quadratic; every lower level is affine-linear in the new slice coefficients, and its coefficient matrix depends only on the corner data (a,b,r), so the rank is constant and consistency is L.b = 0 for a left-nullspace basis L.

level_19.closed_form: P8 = a y^14 (y-r)^2, Q12 = b y^21 (y-r)^3 (a,b,r != 0 forced by the four vertices)
level_19.closed_form_derivation: 8 A B' = 12 A' B  <=>  (B/y^21)^2 = const * (A/y^14)^3;  deg(A/y^14) = 2 and deg(B/y^21) = 3 with nonzero constant terms, so all root multiplicities must be even: A/y^14 = a (y-r)^2 and B/y^21 = b (y-r)^3.
level_19.strict_chart_note: the literal variety has the 4-dimensional component {P8 = 0} (P8 = 0 makes the leading form vanish identically); the component with all four corner coefficients nonzero is the 3-parameter family above

level_18.solution_shape: with k(y) = (tau0 + r*tau1 + r^2*tau2) + (tau1 + r*tau2)*y + tau2*y^2:  P7 = (2a/(3b)) y^12 k(y), Q11 = y^19 (y-r) k(y)

level_17.conclusion: The single consistency condition is the square of a linear form in the three level-18 parameters, hence it defines a codimension-1 locus and is SOLVABLE.  The level-17 block is therefore not empty.

stage5_x_adic_cascade.conclusion: The x-adic cascade is consistent at x-degrees 19, 18 and 17: the only obstruction is a square of a linear form that can be solved for one free parameter.  So no emptiness certificate comes from the top of the cascade.  Diagnostic only; no claim about the remaining x-degrees 16..1 beyond what is stated.

why_not_decisive: EMPTY_BY_SUPPORT is false: (2,0) is attainable; the coefficient of x^2 in det J is exactly a1_0*b2_1, a single nonzero bilinear term from the vertices (1,0) of N(P) and (2,1) of N(Q).
The minimal x-degree of det J is 1, and the x^1 block is three equations in five unknowns with a 3-dimensional solution set; adding a1_0*b2_1 = 1 keeps dimension 3.
Every single-edge leading-form condition is either vacuous (leading form identically zero) or satisfiable; no weight yields an empty leading block.

The strongest weight, w = (2,-1), reduces to 16 equations in 17 unknowns with a triangular elimination down to 6 equations in 7 unknowns; that block is non-empty as a system and its exact-corner-degree part is not resolved by leading data alone.

The x-adic cascade is consistent at x-degrees 19, 18 and 17: its only obstruction there is the square of a linear form and is solvable.  That is positive evidence that the FULL-lattice system may even be non-empty; the vertices-only specialization being empty does not transfer.
what_would_decide: Solve (F0)-(F4) exactly: five univariate-polynomial identities in seven polynomials of degrees 8,8,8,12,12,12,12 (72 coefficients). This is an exact, complete reformulation, not a truncation.
Or run the x-degree-ordered cascade to the bottom: the levels at x-degree <= 6 introduce no new coefficients, so all of the overdetermination (92 equations vs 72 unknowns) sits there.
what_is_not_claimed: No emptiness statement is made.  The verdict is NOT_DECISIVE.
No truncation of the support was used: the analysed support is the full 25 + 47 lattice-point support.
The x-adic cascade analysis covers x-degrees 19, 18 and 17 only; x-degrees 16..1 are not analysed, so no statement about the full system follows from it.
The (F0)-(F4) reformulation is exact and complete, but it is not solved: only its top block (F0) is reduced.
